title: COMPUTE 2025 – Best Practices in Computer Science Education: Ideas Session Report
venue: COMPUTE 2025 – Best Practices track at the ACM COMPUTE Conference
extended_summary:
This paper is not the requested secondary-school writing study on AI-assisted writing feedback. Instead, it is a track-level report from the Best Practices session at COMPUTE 2025, focused on improving computer science education in India. The paper addresses how the computing education community can share practical teaching ideas, redesign programming assignments in response to AI use, and strengthen educator networks.

The paper summarizes ideas generated during Best Practices sessions rather than evaluating a formal intervention. Three themes are covered: classroom activities that support engagement and learning in programming courses, designs for take-home programming assignments that are more resistant to misuse of AI tools, and activities to build a stronger community of computer science educators. Suggested approaches include pair programming, debugging exercises, project-based learning, viva voce assessments, peer review, transparent and guided AI use, and regional educator meetups and resource-sharing platforms.

The context is higher education computer science, explicitly described as "the higher education level" and situated at COMPUTE 2025 held at IIT Ropar in India. Participants were members of the computer science education community, especially educators attending the conference sessions; students are discussed as beneficiaries of the teaching practices, but they were not directly studied as research participants in a formal evaluation.

The paper concludes that the Best Practices track successfully generated many practical ideas for teaching, assessment, and community-building. The authors report positive community feedback and state that iSIGCSE plans to adopt and support these ideas throughout the year. However, the report does not present controlled outcome data, participant-level measures, or evidence of effects on student learning.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided document is a conference track summary and ideas-session report, not an empirical study. It does not present a defined sample, intervention implementation, outcome measurement, or evaluative methodology for a secondary-school writing intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: No causal or descriptive impact estimates are reported for student writing outcomes. The document only discusses community suggestions and broad best-practice ideas, so educational impact is unclear and unmeasured.
